# Following the Example of Geologists, Biologists and Philologists

Messrs.[^1] Dewey, Schiller and their allies, in reaching this general conception of all truth, have only followed the example of geologists, biologists and philologists.[^2] In the establishment of these other sciences, the successful stroke was always to take some simple process actually observable in operation[^3] and then to generalize it, making it apply to all times, and produce great results by summating its effects through the ages.[^4]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as a Theory of Truth]] "Messrs."
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as a Theory of Truth]] "Dewey, Schiller and their allies, in reaching this general conception of all truth, have only followed the example of geologists, biologists and philologists."
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as a Theory of Truth]] "In the establishment of these other sciences, the successful stroke was always to take some simple process actually observable in operation"
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as a Theory of Truth]] "and then to generalize it, making it apply to all times, and produce great results by summating its effects through the ages."
